item.title: MySQLDump - MySQL database backup
item.description:
Using the mysqldump tool, you can back up a local database and restore it to a remote database with the same characteristics, all using a simple command. Next, you’ll see practical examples of using the mysqldump tool to export and import MySQL databases.

Below is an export example:

1

$ mysqldump -u [USERNAME] -p[PASSWORD] [DATABASE-NAME] > dumpfilename.sql

And to import the database:

1

$ mysql -u [USERNAME] -p[PASSWORD] [DATABASE-NAME] < dumpfilename.sql

item.title: Getting to Know and Installing the SAMBA server on LINUX
item.description:
WHAT IS IT?

SAMBA is a server and a set of tools that lets Linux and Windows machines communicate with each other, sharing services (files, directories, printing) through the SMB (Server Message Block)/CIFS (Common Internet File System) protocol, equivalent to the NetBEUI implementation on Windows.

It can also be used as a primary domain controller (PDC), serving as an authentication server for Windows clients.

In most cases, access control and directory display in samba are more detailed and customizable than in Microsoft’s own system.

item.title: How to recreate a .deb from an installed package
item.description:
If you use the Ubuntu operating system or any other distro derived from Debian, you’ve most likely needed to install a program on another machine that wasn’t yours, but when it was time to copy it… where’s the .deb?

If you find the program on the Internet, fine, but what if it’s no longer available for download? What if you don’t have Internet access at the moment?

That’s what “dpkg-repack” is for.

item.title: What is XAMPP and what is it for?
item.description:
Hello, let me introduce you to my favorite package (Apache + PHP + MySQL). This is how I started; today I install them separately.

What is XAMPP?

XAMPP is a package that includes the main open-source servers available, including FTP, the MySQL database and Apache with support for the PHP and Perl languages.
